code: # T and F used as names (here a column name and an argument name) are not reported. fun4 <- function(x){     df <- base::data.frame(T = 1:2, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)     y <- df$T # column named T     z <- base::list(F = 3) # argument named F     base::return(y) } true_false_check(x = fun4) ##  ##  ## AFTER RUNNING saferDev::true_false_check(). ## INSIDE fun4(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN. # If T is defined in the function, its uses are not reported. fun5 <- function(x){     T <- 2     base::return(x + T) } true_false_check(x = fun5) ##  ##  ## AFTER RUNNING saferDev::true_false_check(). ## INSIDE fun5(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN. # Strings and comments are ignored. fun6 <- function(x){     base::return("T") # F } true_false_check(x = fun6) ##  ##  ## AFTER RUNNING saferDev::true_false_check(). ## INSIDE fun6(), EVERYTHING SEEMS CLEAN. # A T used as the whole assigned value is not reported, but a T used as an operand is. fun7 <- function(x, y){     z <- T # not reported     w <- T & y # reported     base::return(w) } true_false_check(x = fun7) ##  ##  ##  ## INSIDE fun7(), SOME SYMBOLS T OR F MUST BE WRITTEN TRUE OR FALSE: ##  ## LINE SYMBOL      CODE ## 4    T       w <- T & y ## function (x, y)  ## { ##     z <- T ##     w <- TRUE & y ##     base::return(w) ## }
